extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 schools, postsecondary institutions, museums), campus administrators, Title IX coordinators, counsel, and policy-makers
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance procedures for recipients
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive preamble and regulatory clarifications describing how 34 CFR part 106 (Title IX) applies to reports of sexual harassment, including scope (students and employees), definitions (actual knowledge), procedural requirements (grievance process, hearings, supportive measures), and protections (retaliation, confidentiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may enforce separate codes of conduct (Title VII/other laws)
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations do not preclude a recipient from enforcing a code of conduct that is separate and apart from what Title IX requires, such as a code of conduct that may address what Title VII requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may proactively address conduct prohibited under Title VII when the conduct does not meet Title IX's definition of sexual harassment; nothing in 34 CFR part 106 may be read in derogation of any individual's rights under Title VII (revises §106.6(f)). Mandatory dismissal for Title IX purposes does not preclude action under another provision of the recipient's code of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment of reports (no favoritism or suppression)
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations apply to all reports of sexual harassment, and a recipient cannot ignore or promote certain reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campus administrators may not ignore or promote certain reports to help or undermine careers; all reports must be handled under the regulations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of retaliation (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: No recipient or other person may intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate against any individual for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.71 added to expressly prohibit retaliation, including coercing witnesses or discriminating against anyone for reporting, participating in, or assisting with investigations, proceedings, or hearings under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory dismissal limited to Title IX purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A mandatory dismissal under §106.45(b)(3)(i) is only for Title IX purposes and does not preclude action under another provision of the recipient's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may still pursue other disciplinary or code-based actions even when a matter is dismissed for Title IX jurisdictional reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge definition for elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'actual knowledge' in §106.30 is revised to include notice to any employee of an elementary or secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A student's report of sexual harassment or notice to any employee of the elementary or secondary school is sufficient to hold the school district liable for a proper response under these final regulations; elementary/secondary schools may still require employees to report to the Title IX Coordinator but notice to any employee triggers the duty to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX protections and grievance processes apply to employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's final regulations apply to employees, and students and employees should have the same protections with respect to regulations addressing sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cannot discern a meaningful justification to treat employees differently than students; grievance process provisions in §106.45 may apply to employees and do not conflict with Title VII; supportive measures are available to any complainant or respondent, including employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will not adopt 'severe or pervasive' employment-only standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not adopt a 'severe or pervasive' standard for the employment context and declines to treat employees differently with respect to the sexual harassment definition applied in Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains reasons throughout the preamble (including First Amendment/academic freedom concerns) for not adopting a different standard for employees; recognizes Title VII may have different standards but sees no inherent conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may provide additional employee rights but must comply with Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations do not preclude a recipients' obligation to honor additional rights negotiated by faculty in any collective bargaining agreement or employment contract, provided such contracts comply with these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may give employees additional or separate rights; the Department has long acknowledged that institutional policies, handbooks, and collective bargaining agreements can create additional rights so long as Title IX obligations are fulfilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures available to all parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures, as defined in §106.30, are available to any complainant or respondent, including employee-complainants and employee-respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations do not restrict supportive measures to students; recipients must offer supportive measures irrespective of whether a complainant files a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on coercing witnesses and interference with participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.71, a faculty member with seniority could not coerce witnesses to provide favorable testimony and no recipient may intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate to interfere with rights under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaliation protections expressly bar coercion of witnesses and other conduct that would interfere with investigation or adjudication of complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department cannot enforce State mandatory reporting laws but encourages compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department encourages all recipients to comply with all laws applicable to the recipient but does not have authority to enforce or administer State laws or State mandatory reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would be a burden for the Department to track all state laws; recipients remain responsible for complying with state mandatory reporting and criminal statutes separate from Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of identities (§106.71) with limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination, including complainants, respondents, alleged perpetrators, and witnesses, except as permitted by FERPA, as required by law, or to carry out the purposes of 34 CFR part 106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality provision added to §106.71; exceptions include FERPA (20 U.S.C. 1232g and 34 CFR part 99), legal requirements, or necessary disclosures to conduct investigations, hearings, or judicial proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisors need not be attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors may be, but are not required to be, attorneys (revisions to §106.45(b)(5)(iv) and §106.45(b)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department clarified advisors do not have to be lawyers to serve as a party's advisor during hearings and cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary will not deem recipient determinations as deliberate indifference simply for differing conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(b)(2) states the Assistant Secretary will not deem a recipient's determination regarding responsibility to be evidence of deliberate indifference solely because the Assistant Secretary would have reached a different determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department will not dictate recipient determinations of responsibility or mandate specific disciplinary sanctions; recipients must describe range of possible disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(b)(1)(vi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to respond promptly and not be deliberately indifferent (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients with actual knowledge of sexual harassment in an education program or activity of the recipient against a person in the United States must respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must act promptly regardless of whether complainant and respondent are students or employees; promptness is also required when respondent is an employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process timeframes and prompt resolution (§106.45(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must include reasonably prompt time frames for the conclusion of the grievance process, including reasonably prompt time frames for filing and resolving appeals and informal resolution processes, if the recipient offers informal resolution processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department requires reasonably prompt timeframes; processes should avoid undue delay even where hearings or cross-examination are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing with cross-examination requirement and accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations include a live hearing with cross-examination requirement for postsecondary institutions (§106.45(b)(6)(i)), and parties may be in separate rooms during the live hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department acknowledges concerns about cost and delay but defends protections; parties will be subjected to cross-examination through a party's advisor; recipient must ensure hearing officers and cross-examiners are competent and qualified as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution process permitted (§106.45(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may facilitate an informal resolution process under §106.45(b)(9) to resolve sexual harassment allegations as between parties, including between employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution is an option recipients may offer; recipients must provide reasonably prompt timeframes for informal resolution if offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients remain free to choose whether to accept Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients choose to receive Federal financial assistance and these final regulations are a condition of that Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipients do not wish to comply with these final regulations (e.g., renegotiating collective bargaining agreements), they may forgo Federal financial assistance rather than being forced into compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients can address conduct under other standards (e.g., 'severe or pervasive')
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in these final regulations precludes a recipient-employer from addressing conduct that is 'severe or pervasive' under a code of conduct for employees to satisfy Title VII obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient-employer may address conduct that meets other legal standards under its own policies even if it does not fall within Title IX's definition for purposes of 34 CFR part 106.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will not require specific disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not require a recipient to impose a specific type of disciplinary sanction on a respondent who is an employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal flexibility: recipients must describe range of possible disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(b)(1)(vi)) but have discretion in selection and are not compelled to impose particular sanctions by the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment status governed by State law; 'student' definition limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'student' in 34 CFR 106.2(r) refers only to that term and does not affect the definition of 'employee' under the final regulations; State law governs employee status and timing of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment status questions (employee vs independent contractor; time of employment) are governed by State law; participation in or attempting to participate in an education program or activity is relevant for whether Title IX applies and for filing a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious institution exemption under 20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An educational institution controlled by a religious organization is exempt from complying with Title IX and these final regulations to the extent that Title IX would not be consistent with the religious tenets of such organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients that qualify may assert a §106.12 exemption; the Department views final regulations as consistent with statutory religious exemptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No differential procedural treatment based on employee type
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient should not be able to treat an allegation of sexual harassment differently based on the type of employee (temporary, part-time, full-time, tenured, at-will) who is reporting or is the subject of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irrespective of position, tenure, part-time status, or at-will status, no employee should be deprived of protections and processes provided by these final regulations; recipients may not impose differential treatment that undermines Title IX protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will construe Title IX to avoid conflict with Title VII obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no inherent conflict between Title VII and Title IX, and the Department will construe Title IX and its implementing regulations in a manner to avoid an actual conflict between an employer's obligations under Title VII and Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department acknowledges different standards and jurisprudence but expects recipients to comply with both where applicable; where jurisdiction overlaps, recipients can implement complementary processes and address issues under multiple authorities as appropriate.
